verses.1: Then, at the age of sixteen, I once again went to Jerusalem, along with Barnabas and Titus.
verses.2: I also went up according to the plan of God. I proclaimed the gospel to them, as I was commanded to do among all nations. But I did not go about empty-handed or without any results.
verses.3: But even Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was forced to leave.
verses.4: But because of those false brothers who came to spy out our freedom that we have in Christ Jesus, so that they might deceive us.
verses.5: So that we might not spend even an hour in this manner, so that the truth of the gospel might not be hidden from you.
verses.6: But those who try to do so… I don’t think anything has changed in that regard. A god doesn’t take any form of human appearance upon himself. After all, those who try to do so don’t really offer anything at all.
verses.7: But on the contrary, they saw that I truly believed in the message of the Ark, just as Peter believed in the message of the circumcision.
verses.8: For he inspired Peter to be sent on a mission of circumcision; he also inspired me to go among the nations.
verses.9: And knowing that this gift was given to me, Jacobus, Kefas, and Ioannes, who thought they were being deceived, they gave me their right hands as a sign of friendship. Thus, we went among the peoples, while they went to the circumcision ceremony.
verses.10: Only for those who are poor, so that we may remember them. This is what I decided to do.
verses.11: And when Kefas arrived in Antiochean, he was met with hostility by those who were against him. He was considered to be a traitor.
verses.12: Before they went there, some people from Jacob came together with the other nations. When they arrived, they sent for themselves and hid from those who were from the circumcision group.
verses.13: And the other Jews also agreed with him in this statement. Thus, Barnabas was also included among them in this agreement.
verses.14: But when I saw that they did not follow the truth of the gospel, I said to Cefas, “If you are a Jew who lives both as a Jew and not as one, how can you force other nations to become Jews?”
verses.15: We are Jews by nature, and we are not sinners from any other nation.
verses.16: And since you know that a person cannot be justified by the works of the law, unless they also believe in Jesus Christ. And we must come to Christ, so that we may be justified by faith in Christ, and not by the works of the law. For by the works of the law, no one can be justified at all.
verses.17: And if they seek to be justified in Christ, yet they themselves are still sinners. Then is Christ a servant of sinners? No, that is not true.
verses.18: For if I build these things again, I indeed become a traitor to myself.
verses.19: For I die by law, in accordance with the law, so that I may live for God. I am united with Christ.
verses.20: I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. Whoever lives now, lives in the flesh; he lives by faith in the Son of God, who has loved me and given himself for me.
verses.21: I do not reject the gift from God. For if justice is based on law, then Christ’s sacrifice was indeed a gift from God.
